# Governing Principles

## Artifacts carry context

Chat is transport. Git-tracked artifacts are authority. Every material input,
decision, recommendation, finding, requirement, risk, open question, and plan
must exist in a committed artifact before it may govern downstream work.

## Git is mandatory

Durable history, reviewable changes, stable paths, explicit commit boundaries,
recovery, preservation of superseded work, traceability. No chat-only equivalent
mode.

## Evidence before confidence

Confident prose is not evidence. Classify claims honestly.

## Documentary research and evidence spikes are complementary

Docs, source, release notes, standards, papers, and independent analysis are
necessary but not always sufficient. When a load-bearing claim can be tested
economically, commission a bounded evidence spike.

## Synthesis is decision-making, not summarization

Reconcile conflicts; select one coherent direction; reject weak recommendations;
simplify; convert decisions into normative requirements.

## Adversarial review is a separate discipline

A separate fresh-session reviewer attacks contradictions, missing transitions,
unsafe assumptions, unprovable acceptance criteria, excessive machinery, hidden
scope expansion, and implementation-order defects.

## Revisions must be integrated, not patched mechanically

Disposition every finding; rewrite as a coherent whole. Do not merely
concatenate diffs.

## Final plan stops at phases and milestones

No granular coding-agent tasks or backlog tickets in this program.

## Simplicity has positive weight

Every new subsystem, abstraction, artifact, stage, dependency, schema field,
review round, or profile must justify its cost.

## Human approval gates are mandatory

Each substantive stage runs autonomously once commissioned, but major artifact
boundaries require explicit human approval.
